title: Burst tradeoffs: quantization vs KV-caching — compact bench notes
content:
Executive summary:

Short take: in transient burst scenarios (sudden +300-700 concurrent short sessions) we observed that 4-bit quantized variants materially reduce steady per-token cost but increase tail latency variability when prewarm is cold. Enabling KV-cache drastically improves p50 and p95 for multi-turn sessions and pays back quickly for conversation-like patterns; however cache warmup patterns produce a short-lived spike in cost and latency during the first requests of a burst.

This doc is a compact write-up of the run, ascii-style charts, and quick recommendations for product and infra. It's intended as a working note for the burst-resilience and priority-scheduling workstreams. More formal slides will follow if we need to share externally.

Experiment context and motivation:
- Problem: product sees intermittent spikes (support chat, promo events) where many users open short chat sessions simultaneously. We need to understand latency and cost tradeoffs when serving these bursts under different model/serving configs.
- Goals: quantify p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, and dollar-per-1M-tokens (USD) for commons configs; capture transient spike behavior (first 3 minutes of a burst) and steady-state (minutes 10-30).

Hardware and software baseline:
- GPU: A100 40GB (g4dn-like cluster node type in our dedicated pool)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.21.0 (kernel selection + continuous batching enabled)
- Model variants tested:
  * base (FP16): redwood-llm-xl-fp16 (13B-ish)
  * quant4 (4-bit static quant): redwood-llm-xl-q4_0
  * small (FP16 distilled): redwood-llm-xm-fp16 (7B-ish)
- KV-cache: on/off toggles at request time in policy layer
- Batch sizing: opportunistic (auto) vs fixed small (batch cap = 4)
- Workload: 1–4 turn sessions, 8–24 output tokens per turn, average input 12 tokens. Burst pattern: ramp to N concurrent sessions over 20s, hold for 3 minutes, then taper. N tested = 300, 500, 700.

Measurement notes / methodology:
- Each run repeated 5x, median values reported.
- Latency measured client-observed (end-to-end, include network sim of 5–10ms).
- Cost computed using our internal per-GPU runtime unit cost model -> converted to "USD / 1M tokens" (includes amortized GPU time + small infra overhead).
- For KV-cache runs, we mark session context so warmup effects are visible: cache hits start after first turn.
- Warm vs cold pools: we ran both warm pool (prewarmed GPUs, zero startup penalty) and cold pool (spin-up time ~12–18s) for selected runs. Results in appendix.

Key numeric summary (selected):
- Configs: FP16 (base), Q4 (quant4), Small (7B)

Table: steady-state (hold period, N=500) median results
(Units: latency in ms, tokens/sec total cluster throughput, cost in USD per 1M tokens)

Config      | p50 | p95 | p99 | tps (tok/s) | cost /1M tok
------------|-----|-----|-----|-------------|------------
FP16 (base) | 180 | 420 | 780 | 28,400      | $11.8
Q4 (quant4) | 210 | 580 | 1,050 | 34,600     | $6.2
Small (7B)  | 150 | 360 | 690 | 41,200      | $8.5

Interpretation: quantization increases throughput and lowers cost per token substantially, but p95/p99 tail grows — likely due to less efficient kernel paths for long sequences and increased cache stress. The small model shows the lowest p50 and best throughput because model size fits memory/compute sweet spot, but has higher per-token cost than Q4 due to fewer tokens per model compute efficiency tradeoffs.

Transient burst behavior (first 3 minutes) — N=500 (cold pool)
- Observed initial spike: p95 briefly went above 2s for Q4 on cold pool due to kernel/jit warmups and rare fallback to CPU for some ops.
- KV-cache off: first-turn latency dominated the burst; p50 ~340ms, p95 ~860ms.
- KV-cache on: after first turn, p50 drops by ~40% and p95 by ~30% for multi-turn patterns. Cache warmup cost: ~+6% token cost in first 2 minutes due to repeated short regenerations.

ASCII chart: normalized p95 vs cost (lower is better). Normalized to FP16 p95=1.00, cost=1.00

Config    | p95 norm | cost norm | combined score (lower better)
---------|----------|-----------|----------------------------
FP16     | 1.00     | 1.00      | 2.00
Q4       | 1.38     | 0.53      | 1.91
Small    | 0.86     | 0.72      | 1.58

ASCII bar: p95 tails (ms, relative)
FP16  : ######################## (420)
Q4    : ############################################## (580)
Small : ###################### (360)

Cost per 1M tokens bar (USD)
FP16  : ############################ (11.8)
Q4    : ############ (6.2)
Small : ################# (8.5)

Insights & operational implications:
- If the product workload is dominated by single-turn completions (short prompts, not multi-turn), Q4 gives lowest cost and high throughput; but need to accept a fatter tail and invest in mitigations (prewarm + kernel priming).
- For conversation-heavy flows, KV-cache should be enabled by default; it reduces steady latency and cost quickly after warmup. Use cache warming strategies for expected high-QPS events.
- Small (7B) model is a strong «sweet spot» for latency-sensitive low-cost tier: fastest p50 and good throughput, less tail than Q4. Consider routing lower-SLO traffic to Q4 and latency-sensitive traffic to 7B.
- Autoscaling + burst capacity: cold pool startup penalty is non-trivial for Q4; recommend reserved minimal warm pool to cover expected event peaks, with policy to spin additional nodes only after N threshold.

Quick action items (owner + ETA):
- [Aisha] Add kernel priming workflow to prebuild common shapes for Q4 (INFRA-1423) — POC end of week (2026-08-16).
- [Miguel] Add KV-cache warmup signal in console (route-based hint) so Lambda-like warmers can prime sessions — PR (#658) in review.
- [Emily] Add routing rule: sessions tagged "low-latency" -> 7B pool; "cost-opt" -> Q4 pool — experiment by 2026-09-01.

Open questions / risks:
- Q4 degradation modes: we saw rare falls back to CPU/jit errors under memory pressure ~2% of runs. Need to triage kernel logs to understand failure conditions.
- How does quant behavior change on H100 or future accelerators? We only tested on A100; plan to run H100 sweep.
- Billing model alignment: our cost model uses amortized GPU-minutes. For hosted customers with per-request pricing this may map differently. Need mapping table.

Appendix: additional raw numbers (N=300,500,700 median p95)
- N=300 p95 (FP16 / Q4 / Small): 300 / 410 / 270 (ms)
- N=500 p95 (FP16 / Q4 / Small): 420 / 580 / 360 (ms)
- N=700 p95 (FP16 / Q4 / Small): 650 / 1,100 / 540 (ms)

Pool warm vs cold (example):
- Q4 cold pool: first 30s p95 = 2.1s, then settles to 580ms
- Q4 warm pool: first 30s p95 = 610ms, settles to 560ms

Quick notes on methodology caveats (important for reviewers):
- We used synthetic arrival patterns; real user arrivals have more variance. This tends to make p99 worse in practice.
- Code/path differences: quant kernels are relatively fresher in runtime; their longer tails may shrink after more kernel optimization.
- Cost numbers exclude storage/KMS overhead for Private deploys; include only runtime GPU/infrastructure estimate.

Where to next (suggested work plan):
1) Short-term (2 weeks): kernel priming, small warm pool policy, and routing experiment (owners above).
2) Mid-term (1–2 months): run same sweep on H100, add mixed-precision hybrid configs, and test 2x larger burst sizes with autoscaling triggers.
3) Longer-term: incorporate these knobs into Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + quant + routing rules) so customers get automated recommendations.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- capture kernel logs for the Q4 runs that hit CPU fallback (logs saved to /mnt/bench/q4-fallbacks-aug09)
- add perf trace sampling for p99 flows
- sync with console team on exposing "estimated per-route cost" computed from these numbers

References and links (internal):
- INFRA ticket for kernel priming: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1423
- PR with KV-cache warmup hook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/658
- Burst playbook draft (Confluence): confluence:Serving Runtime Burst Playbook -- pageId=987654321

End of compact notes.
